sentences.text:
Mr. Sanjay Kumar Pathak, Learned Standing Counsel has referred to the directions of this Court dated 13.02.2023, consequent to which it appears that a meeting was held by the concerned officials under the Chairmanship of the Additional Chief Secretary on 06.03.2023 and Annexure R-2 /2 is filed along with the status report dated 10.05.2023, wherein inter alia the following observations were made:
5.

In the meeting held on 06.03.2023 under the chairmanship of the Addl. Chief Secretary, Land & Building Department, it is observed that the petitioners have concealed the material fact from the Hon'ble Court qua the passing of order dated 21.10. 2015 by LAC as it was submitted in para no. 10 of writ petition No. 8404/2015 that the LAC did not pass any order pursuant to judgment dated 20.04.2015 whereby a direction was given to treat the writ petition as representation for seeking interest under Section 34 of the LA Act, 1894.
6.
It is also observed in the meeting that the order dated 21.10.2015 is still in existence and in supersession of the same no formal order
This is a digitally signed order.

Further, DDA representatives indicated that DDA is not liable to pay any additional interest as the entire compensation amount already stands deposited with LAC, and LAC has earlier concluded that no interest is payable to the petitioners.
2.

Learned counsel for the petitioner on the other hand has referred to the copy of the Khata Khatoni of the land in question which was acquired by the Government wherein on 06.12.2005, it was recorded that there were some inter-se disputes amongst the members of the family.

It is urged that in view of the said fact, the Collector was duty bound to exercise his duties under Section 31 & 34 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
3.

It is further pointed out by Mr. Mathur, learned counsel for the petitioner that the proceedings had taken place before the Land Acquisition Collector on 07.07.2017, whereby the petitioners were made entitled to grant of interest from the date of taking possession of the land in dispute on 23.11.2005 till the date of release of compensation on 13.10.2013 although the award is dated 17.08.2005.
4.

It is also pointed out that subsequent to the decision taken by the competent authority on 07.07.2017, there were two letters written by the concerned officials from the same Department dated 21 September 2017 and 13 November 2017 whereby the concerned authority was called upon to release the amount of interest to the petitioners.

5. The long and short of the submission of the learned counsel for the respondent no.1 is that order dated 21.10.2015 was concealed by the petitioner in writ petition no. 8404 / 2015 resulting in direction of this by the DB of this Court dated 18.04.2017 and resulting in the preparation of notings on 07.07.2017.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 14/12/2023 at 23:35:50 6.

Therefore, this Court directs the respondent no.1 to bring the entire original file concerning this matter before this Court as it needs to be looked into as to under what facts and circumstances, the order dated 21.10.2015 came to be passed by the LAC and whether there were issued any notice to the petitioners and whether any replies were filed by any of the varying parties.
7. The Competent Authority shall also appear in person before this Court on the next date of hearing.

8. Re-notify on 29.04.2024.
DHARMESH SHARMA, J.
